item.title: People streamed the Winter Olympics in Canada way more than ever before
item.description: The Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Olympics have come to a close, but how many Canadians tuned in to watch the Games?

item.title: Vancouver's largest cafe gets opening date
item.description: After first reporting on the location last year, C Market Coffee has shared the opening date for what will be Vancouver's largest cafe.

item.title: Stranded hiker rescued from snowy North Shore mountain with only 1 percent battery life
item.description: A winter visit to Mt. Seymour ended in a nighttime rescue for a stranded hiker. But it could have been a lot more harrowing.

item.title: Canadian sushi restaurant set to open its first Calgary location
item.description: Toro Toro, the Toronto-born sushi restaurant, has revealed it is on its way west with its new Calgary location at 39 Crowfoot Terrace NW.

item.title: Is there a DeBrusk trade to be made with Edmonton Oilers and Vancouver Canucks?
item.description: Could there be a Jake DeBrusk trade brewing between the Edmonton Oilers and Vancouver Canucks ahead of the deadline?

item.title: There's 'renewed' trade interest in Vancouver Canucks' Elias Pettersson: report
item.description: The Vancouver Canucks have a week and a half until the NHL trade deadline. Is there any chance they pull the trigger on a Pettersson trade?

item.title: City of Surrey sets aside $200 million for new 10,000-seat indoor arena
item.description: City of Surrey is preparing to spend about $200 million from 2026 to 2030 on building the new Surrey City Centre Arena.

item.title: Yes, that cottage from 'Heated Rivalry' can be booked on Airbnb
item.description: Fans of "Heated Rivalry" will soon be able to book the Barlochan Cottage in Muskoka, Ontario, made popular by the Heated Rivalry show.

item.title: Burrard Inlet's lift rail bridge stuck, unable to open for large ships to pass through Second Narrows for days
item.description: A malfunction of the critical Second Narrows Rail Bridge of Burrard Inlet in Metro Vancouver has halted major marine traffic.

item.title: Vancouver's first FIFA World Cup decorations go up outside former Hudson's Bay building
item.description: The empty storefronts of the former Hudson's Bay building in downtown Vancouver are now covered with official 2026 FIFA World Cup branding.
